key_insight: WC–Co–Cr coating performance depends on powder morphology and spray method: detonation spraying favors hardness, while HVOF provides a dense, uniform coating with low friction.
engineering_relevance: Selecting the powder and spraying process can help tailor wear-resistant coatings for machine parts exposed to intensive friction and high loads.
method: Compare detonation-sprayed and HVOF WC–Co–Cr coatings.
Examine powder morphology and coating microstructure using SEM and EDS.
Evaluate coating microhardness and tribological behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average microhardness of 1449 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and a friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF coatings.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify test conditions, variability, or wear-rate data, limiting direct prediction of service performance.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
